_comment: Doomscroll — the roguelike campaign. Everything the mode knows lives here;
src/game/doomscroll/ contains the rules that read it, never the content.
Two acts ship. The design lists four, but acts 3 and 4 end in faction bosses
whose rule twists need effect ops the DSL does not have yet (see
data/cards/bosses.json). A finale with a twist that silently does nothing is
worse than a shorter run that ends in a real one, so acts 3-4 arrive with the
ops they need. The act list is data — adding them is an edit to this file.
Two leaders are unlocked, exactly as the design specifies; the rest arrive

leaders.name: Lumi, Starcall
leaders.blurb: Halo and Pulse. Wide boards, loud buffs, and a fanbase that will not be reasoned with.

leaders.name: The Blue Screen Baron
leaders.blurb: Veil and Cinder. Trades you did not agree to, in a font you cannot read.

acts.name: The Shallow End
acts.blurb: Everyone is nice here. That is the first warning sign.
_floorPlan: One node per floor, chosen from what your last node connects to.
Floor 0 is always a fight so the act opens on the game itself, and the
floor before the boss is always a Touch Grass Break so nobody arrives at
the Main Event with no way to have healed. Genre convention, and it

boss.name: Prisma, the Final Encore
boss.twistText: While Prisma holds three or more characters, every one of them has +1 attack.

acts.name: The Trending Depths
acts.blurb: The recommendations stop being recommendations and start being instructions.

boss.name: DJ Last Call
boss.twistText: Every Afterparty trigger the boss has fires twice.

acts.name: The Dead Internet
acts.blurb: Nothing down here was posted by a person. It is all still arguing.

boss.name: GLITCHLORD_EXE
boss.twistText: Every third card you draw costs (1) more. The count is public — watch the Corrupted Feed counter.

_note: Act 4 is the optional true finale, and it is one fight — no map to walk,
no shop, no rest. You arrive holding three Signal Fragments or you do not
arrive at all, and the run's last decision was made two acts ago when you
chose to walk into an Elite instead of around it.
acts.name: The First Signal
acts.blurb: The seven strands are already leaning towards each other. You are the last thing between them.

boss._deckNote: The Meme Collective, because the Second Fracture camp's whole fear is that a reassembled Signal dissolves every subculture into an undifferentiated hum — and the Collective is the faction that already sounds like that. Chairperson Nobody is anonymous, plural and everywhere, which is the closest a real deck gets to 'all seven strands at once'.
boss.name: THE FIRST SIGNAL
boss.twistText: It takes one thing back each turn, in a fixed order you can see coming: your leader's Current rotates, then you discard a card, then your costliest character is Banished until your next turn.

_artifactComment: RUN-level ones change health, prices, rewards or the map economy, and the run
BATTLE-level ones ('battlePatch') are a CardPatch applied to the run leader's
card for every fight, carried in MatchConfig.cardOverrides. That is what makes
them the player's alone: the leader card belongs to one seat, whereas a
balance override is one rulebook for both — 'your Fixation costs 2' written
as a balance override would discount the opponent's too.
Still absent, deliberately: 'Ancient Meme Grimoire' (Viral copies cost 2 less)
and 'Foam Finger' (Parasocial grants +2/+2) need a modifier layer the DSL does
not have, and 'The Algorithm's Favor' (look at the top 3 and reorder) would
need a scry the player actually controls — the scry op shuffles. An artifact
whose tooltip lies is worse than a smaller artifact pool.

_upgradesComment: Anything NOT listed here takes the default in data.ts: characters get +1/+1,
everything else costs (1) less. That default is deliberate — 195 authored
upgrades is how this feature would ship half-empty, with the unauthored cards
quietly upgrading into themselves. The loader proves every collectible card's
upgrade actually changes the card, so a hole in this table is a load error
rather than a Rest node that does nothing.
List a card here when +1/+1 or cost-1 is the boring answer — usually to grant
the card's own Current's signature keyword, which the design names as one of

events.title: Sponsored Post Offer
events.text: A brand you have never heard of would like you to hold their product at a 40 degree angle for four seconds.

choices.label: Take the deal
choices.detail: +120 run-Clout, and 4 damage you will describe as "burnout".

choices.label: Stay independent
choices.detail: Add a card to your deck.

events.title: Abandoned Group Chat
events.text: Four hundred unread messages. The last one is from someone asking if you are alright. It is two years old.

choices.label: Read all of it
choices.detail: 6 damage, and an artifact falls out of the archive.

events.title: The Algorithm Blesses You
events.text: One post, for no reason anybody can explain, reaches nine hundred thousand people. None of them follow you afterwards.

choices.label: Ride the wave
choices.detail: Add a card to your deck.

events.title: Ratio'd
events.text: A stranger's four-word reply is outperforming your post forty to one. They have a cartoon frog avatar and no other posts.

events.title: Cursed Recommendation
events.text: The feed serves you something with no caption, no sound and 2.3 million views.

choices.label: Watch the whole thing
choices.detail: 3 damage, and you come out holding an artifact.

events.title: Unsolicited Feedback
events.text: Someone with 12 followers explains, at length and with diagrams, which of your cards is holding you back.

choices.label: They are right
choices.detail: Remove a card from your deck.

events.title: The Director's Cut
events.text: An archivist has been quietly re-rendering your old posts at a resolution nobody had in the first place. She will do one more, or she will hand you the raw files and let you sell them.

choices.label: Let her finish one
choices.detail: Remaster a card in your run deck.

choices.label: Take the raw files
choices.detail: +90 Clout, and 3 damage carrying the drive home.

events.title: Old Account Recovered
events.text: You remember the password. Everything you posted at nineteen is still there, publicly, with timestamps.

choices.label: Repost the classics
choices.detail: Add a card to your deck.

events.title: Scheduled Maintenance
events.text: The whole platform is down. The status page is also down. The status page for the status page says "operational".

choices.label: Post through it
choices.detail: 3 damage, +90 run-Clout, and a permanent reputation as the one who kept going.
